_comment: Frozen contract for the navigate-the-channel task.
Set from FOUR runs of the unmodified configuration, not one. The first
version of this file was written from a single run that measured 0.380 m
of clearance, and put the floor at 0.25 m. Three further runs came back
at 0.320, 0.245 and 0.376 -- so that floor would have failed a perfectly
good run on the very next commit. The spread is sd 0.063 m on a mean of
0.330 m, which is 4x what the open-water benchmark suite showed; that
suite parked its goals in open water, and threading a 2.4 m gate is a
much noisier thing to measure.
'require' is pass/fail. Every new piece of work must leave these true.
'drift_warn' is reported and never fatal, because rebuilding course
geometry moves absolute numbers by construction; a harness that reds on
the first legitimate edit is a harness that gets switched off.
min_clearance_fraction is the term that survives a geometry change. It
normalises the measured clearance by the most the hull could possibly
clear the tightest gate by if it threaded the exact centreline --
(free_water - beam)/2, which is 0.65 m for the 2.40 m gates. Widening or
narrowing a gate moves the numerator and the denominator together, so
the criterion means the same thing before and after. The floor of 0.20 is
mean - 3sd expressed as a fraction (0.217), rounded down: it binds on a
real degradation and not on the noise.
gates_transited is a fraction of gates_total rather than an absolute
count, so adding or removing a gate cannot silently weaken the contract.
